sentences.text: This claim petition is filed under the provisions of Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death of Anil S/o. Late Shiva caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioners case are as under:
It is the case of the petitioners that on 13.08.2021 at about 9.15 am., when Sri.Anil (hereinafter referred to as deceased) was riding his Motor Cycle bearing Reg.
No.PY-01- BF-8119 along with his friend and one sister from Badubanahalli to Ankanahalli, Ankanahalli post, Kodagu, at that time, one Ashok Leyland bearing Reg.No.KA-13-C-3461 came from opposite road driven by its driver with high speed SCCH - 26 3 MVC No.4025/2021 in a rash and negligent manner without following traffic rules and dashed to the deceased's motor cycle.
Due to impact, the deceased fell down sustained head injury and died on the spot.
Immediately deceased was shifted to Government Hospital, Shanivarasante and conducted the post mortem.
The petitioners have spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards incidental charges.
3. Further it is the case of the Petitioners that prior to the accident, deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 27 years, he was doing Tailoring work and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to his death, petitioners put to lot of mental agony, untold misery and lost earning member of the family.
The Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle
are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, they have prayed to award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- from the respondents.
4. The notice of the petition has been duly served on Respondent No.1 and 2 and they have appeared before this tribunal and filed their respective written statement.
Respondent No.1 has filed his written statement by contending that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further contended that the policy was in force at the time of accident hence, he has no liability to pay any compensation to the petitioners arising out of the alleged accident.

Further he denies the involvement of the Ashok Leyland bearing Reg.No.KA-13-C-3461 in the alleged accident and contending that, accident occurred only due to sole negligence of the deceased himself who was riding the motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner, with triple riding and without wearing a helmet.
Further he denied the income and avocation of the deceased.
With these contentions he has prayed to reject the claim petition.

Manjula vs Anil Kumar on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3626251/
2 6.
Respondent No.2 has filed its written statement by contending that, petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.
Further denies the involvement of the vehicle and manner of the accident.
Further it has contended that the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.

Further contended that, the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.PY-01-BF-8119 was riding the SCCH - 26 5 MVC No.4025/2021 same without wearing helmet, without having valid and effective driving licence on the date of accident.
Further it has admitted the issuance of Insurance in favour of the Goods vehicle bearing reg. No.KA-13-C-3461.
Further it has contended that the owner of the vehicle or the police have not complied with the mandatory provisions of the IMV Act after the accident.
It has also contended that the driver of the insured vehicle has not holding valid and effective driving license.
Further it specifically contended that, rider of the motor cycle was riding it with two pillion riders hence, on this grounds alone the petition is liable to be dismissed.
Further it has contended that if any compensation is awarded, the rate of interest may be restricted to 6% p.a.
With these contentions he has prayed to reject the claim petition.

7. On the basis of the above pleadings of both the parties, my predecessor in office has framed the following issues :
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that, SCCH - 26 6 MVC No.4025/2021 deceased Anil S/o Late Shiva, aged about 27 years, was dies in a road traffic accident that occurred on 13.08.2021 at about 09.15 a.m. deceased was riding of the motor cycle bearing Registration No.PY-01-BF-8119 when he reached Badubanahalli village, Ankanahalli post, Kodagu, at that time, the driver of the Ashok Leyland bearing Reg.No.KA-13-C-3461 drove in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased's motor cycle.

As a result deceased sustained fatal injuries and died, as mentioned in claim petition ?
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?

If so, from which respondent ?
3. What order or award?
8. The Petitioner No.1 has got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 13 documents as Ex's.P1 to 13.
On the other hand, the respondent has not adduced any evidence.
9. Heard the arguments from both sides.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

Learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has filed citation reported in MFA No.6227/2008(MV).
10.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly Affirmative SCCH - 26 7 MVC No.4025/2021 Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
Manjula vs Anil Kumar on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3626251/
3 REASONS 11. ISSUE No.1: It is the case of PW.1 that on 13.08.2021 at about 9.15 am., when Sri.Anil (hereinafter referred to as deceased) was riding his Motor Cycle bearing Reg. No.PY-01-BF-8119 along with his friend and one sister from Badubanahalli to Ankanahalli, Ankanahalli post, Kodagu,

at that time, one Ashok Leyland bearing Reg.No.KA-13-C-3461 came from opposite road driven by its driver with high speed in a rash and negligent manner without following traffic rules and dashed to the deceased's motor cycle.
Due to impact, he fell down sustained head injury and died on the spot.
Immediately he was shifted to Government Hospital, Shanivarasante and conducted the post mortem.
12. On the other hand, it is the contention of Respondent No.2 that the insured vehicle has been implicated in collusion with concerned persons to get wrongful gain to the petitioners.

Therefore,
the burden is on SCCH - 26 8 MVC No.4025/2021 the petitioners to prove the actionable negligence on the part of driver of the offending Goods vehicle.
As already stated supra the Petitioner No.1 has examined herself as PW.1.
She has filed affidavit for her chief examination and re-iterated the entire petition averments.

She has got marked 13 documents as Ex.P.1 to P.13.
13.

From the evidence on record it can be seen that after receipt of complaint lodged by one of the pillion rider, the Shanivarasanthe police have registered FIR in Crime No.65/2021 against the driver of Good vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-C-3461 for the offenses punishable u/s.279, 337 and 304-A of IPC.
After due investigation the police have filed charge-sheet against the driver of the offending Goods vehicle for the offenses punishable u/s.279, 337 and 304-A of IPC.

Ex.P.2 is the spot mahazar wherein it is described as the driver of the Goods vehicle drove the same in rash and negligent manner towards right side and dashed to the left side coming bike and due to that impact the rider of the motor cycle died at spot.
And also described that right side part of the motor cycle fully damaged.
Ex . P.3
SCCH - 26 9 MVC No.4025/2021 is the rough sketch and it shows that the accident took place at Badubanahalli village - Ankanahalli at edge of the road.
Ex.P.5 is the inquest, IMV report marked at Ex.P.8 which shows that the accident occurred not due to any mechanical defects of both motor vehicles.

Ex.P.9 is the post mortem report of the deceased and as per this document,
the cause of death is due to shock and hemorrhage, multiple injuries sustained as a result of road traffic accident.
Though the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has cross examined PW.1 but he has failed to elicit anything from her to disbelieve her version.
Therefore, there is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is collusive or defective.

14. Respondent No.2- Insurance Company contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence of the deceased who rode the motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner without wearing helmet with two pillion riders.
Further contended that, false complaint was foisted against the insured vehicle.
PW.1 has denied the same during cross examination and contended that it was the negligence of the SCCH - 26 10 MVC No.4025/2021 driver of the Goods vehicle itself.
The FIR and charge sheet both are filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Except the suggestion during cross examination and contention in the written statement of the Respondent, they have not produced any documentary evidence.
In the absence of documents to prove the negligence of the Goods vehicle driver, it is held that it was the sole negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Manjula vs Anil Kumar on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3626251/
4
Police have filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle after complete investigation and the said charge sheet is not at all challenged by both the Respondents.
15. The evidence of PW-1 corroborates with the documents produced by her.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compared to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the chapter in M.V.Act dealing with compensation is a SCCH - 26 11 MVC No.4025/2021 benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
Therefore, based on the above discussion, I hold that the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-C-3461 is proved.
As such, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
16. ISSUE No.2:
PW.1 has produced Adhar card of herself, petitioner No.2 and her deceased son as per Ex.P.10, 11 and 13.
From these documents it is clear that Petitioners No.1 and 2 are legal heirs and they are dependent on the income of deceased.
Hence, Petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for compensation under the head loss of dependency.
17. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY:-
PW.1 has produced the notarized copy of Aadhar card of deceased at Ex.P.13.
As per this document he was born on 03.03.1993.
Therefore, as on the date of accident he was 28 years.

As per the principles laid down by their Lordships in 2009 ACJ 1298 (Sarla Verma Vs Delhi Transport Corporation), the multiplier applicable to the present case is '17'.
18.

sentences.text: According to PW.1 her deceased son was doing SCCH - 26 12 MVC No.4025/2021 Tailoring work and earning monthly income of Rs.25,000/-.
As PW.1 has not produced any document to prove the income of deceased.
In the absence of proof of avocation and income, this tribunal has to consider notional income for calculating the compensation.
As per the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, the notional income of the deceased is taken as Rs.15,000/- as the accident took place in the year 2021.

19. As per the Hon'ble Apex court reported in a decision reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court cases 680 (National Insurance company Ltd., Vs Pranay Sethi and others), 40% of income is to be added towards future prospects as the deceased was self employed and he is below 40 years.

entities.text: (2017) 16 Supreme Court cases 680 (National Insurance company Ltd., Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore,
40% of Rs.15,000/- works out to Rs.6,000/-.
Therefore, the total income of the deceased works out to Rs.21,000/- (Rs.15,000/- + Rs.6,000/-).
Since the both Petitioners were dependants on the deceased and the deceased was bachelor as such,  of total income is to be deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased.
of Rs.21,000/- works-out to Rs.10,500/-.
Income for SCCH - 26 13 MVC No.4025/2021 consideration is Rs.10,500/- (Rs.21,000/- (-) Rs.10,500/-).
Annual income works out to Rs.1,26,000/- (10,500/- x 12).
Appropriate multiplier is "17".
Thus loss of dependency works-out to Rs.21,42,000/- (1,26,000 x 17).

20. Further, as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs.
Pranay Sethi and Others, amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years under the following conventional heads.

5 filial consortium, Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- towards Funeral expenses.
21.

The calculation table stands as follows :-
1 Loss of dependency Rs. 21,42,000=00 2 Loss of filial consortium Rs. 44,000=00 to petitioner No.1 3 Loss of estate Rs. 16,500=00 4
Funeral expenses Rs. 16,500=00 GRAND TOTAL Rs. 22,19,000=00
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.22,19,000/-.

22. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY: The SCCH - 26 14 MVC No.4025/2021 learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has produced citation reported in MFA No.6227/2008 (MV) (Usman Sheriff @ Thabroz Vs. The National Insurance Co., Ltd., and another) with regard to the contributory negligence on the part of deceased.

entities.text: Usman Sheriff @ Thabroz Vs. The National Insurance Co., Ltd., and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
But during the course of cross examination of PW.1,
respondent No.2 has not elicited anything about the triple riding to prove the negligence or violation of policy.
Even though, only on the ground that deceased along with two pillion riders were proceeding on motor cycle and itself is not sufficient to prove the negligent act on the part of deceased.
Except triple riding nothing is proved to show that triple riding contributed to the accident.

23. The respondent No.1 is the owner of offending and respondent No.2 is insurer of the offending Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-C-3461 and it is admitted fact that as on the date of the accident, the offending vehicle was having valid insurance policy.
Therefore respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6%
From the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 'Partly affirmative'.
24. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
-: ORDER :-
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
 The petitioners are entitled for  compensation of Rs.22,19,000/- (Rupees twenty-two Lakhs nineteen thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, the respondent No.2 being insurer of offending Goods vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within one months from the date of this order.

6

On deposit of the award amount together SCCH - 26 16 MVC No.4025/2021 with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 60%
 Petitioner No.2 - 40%

Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 and 2, a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in their name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to them on verification.
However the said Petitioner No.1 and 2 are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- Draw an award accordingly.

Funeral expenses Rs. 16,500=00 GRAND TOTAL Rs. 22,19,000=00
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.22,19,000/-.
Therefore respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6%
From the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 'Partly affirmative'.
